_comment: The politics engine (M6): history at world creation and the world moving on while you play. rates are chances per year (scaled to the time step). lifespan multiplies ages by race (a dwarf of 140 is like a human of 40). reign: years a ruler usually lasts [min, max] by race. text: the words for each kind of event, used in the chronicle and in news ({slots} filled by code). dragons, artifacts and legends furnish the deep past.

war_reasons.trade: the trade roads and their tolls

old: in their sleep, full of years
murder: at the hands of their own guards
accident: in a fall from a horse
when a tower stair gave way

signs: The trees here stand burned and branchless, in a swathe a mile wide.
There are bones in the grass: cattle, and not only cattle.
Nothing sings here. The quiet has weight to it.
The rock is glazed black in places, as if a furnace had breathed on it.
A dead sheep lies half-eaten and untouched by crows, who know better.

fates: was buried with its last bearer in {site}
was carried into {site} and never came out
was stolen, and no one knows where it went
is said to lie somewhere in {site}

deeds: held the bridge at {place} alone against a warband
led the survivors of {place} through the winter
rode into {site} and did not return
walked out of the plague year alive and healed the sick
betrayed {faction} and was cursed for it
was the last of their line

succession: {old} died {cause}. The {seat} went to {new}, {relation}, with the usual grumbling.
They buried {old}, dead {cause}, and put {new}, {relation}, in the {seat} before the month was out.
crisis: {old} died {cause}, leaving no heir. {new} of {house} took the {seat}, and not everyone agreed.
When {old} died {cause} without an heir, {new} of {house} seized the {seat}.
{old} died {cause} with no heir, and {new} of {house} was quickest to the {seat}.
With {old} dead {cause} and no child to follow, the {seat} went to {new} of {house}, and the lawyers went to work.
elected: {old} died {cause}, and {faction} raised {new} in their place.
{faction} met after {old} died {cause}, argued for a week, and settled on {new}.
gang_ended: {old} ended on a rope, and what was left of {faction} went its own way.
With {old} dead {cause}, nobody could hold {faction} together.
war: It came to war between {attacker} and {defender}, over {reason}, as everyone had said it would.
battle: {loser} lost a battle to {winner} near {place}, and left many dead.
There was a battle near {place}. {winner} held the ground at the end of it; {loser} did not.
siege: {attacker} sat down before the walls of {place}.
The lines went up around {place}, and {attacker} settled in to wait.
taken: {place} fell to {attacker} after a long siege.
{place} opened its gates to {attacker}, in the end.
sacked: {place} was put to the sword by {attacker}.
What {attacker} did in {place} is still not spoken of plainly.
relieved: {attacker} broke off the siege of {place} and went home.
The lines around {place} came up, and the country breathed again.
peace: {a} and {b} put their names to a peace{terms}.
The fighting between {a} and {b} stopped{terms}, which suited neither of them.
rebellion: The banners of {rebel} came down off {liege}'s walls.
freedom: {liege} could not bring {rebel} to heel, and let them go.
{rebel} made their freedom stick, and {liege} let it lie.
{liege} spent three seasons on {rebel} and then stopped spending.
crushed: The rebellion of {rebel} ended in blood.
{liege} put down {rebel}, and hung the leaders where the roads meet.
{rebel} rose, and {liege} saw to it that nobody rose again for a while.
plague: It came to {place} in the spring; {deaths} were dead by the turn of the year.
{place} shut its gates against the sickness and lost {deaths} anyway.
famine: Famine in the lands of {faction}: the harvest failed.
A hungry year in {faction}'s lands, and bread dear everywhere.
The harvest failed in {faction}'s lands and bread went out of reach.
A thin year for {faction}: seed corn eaten, and the roads full of people looking for work.
raid: {tribe} came down on {place} in the night.
{tribe} took what they liked out of {place} and went.
{place} was raided by {tribe}; the cattle went with them.
burned: There is nothing standing in {place} that {tribe} did not leave standing on purpose.
cult: Whispers began of a cult of {god} near {place}.
People went missing near {place}; some said a cult of {god} was to blame.
Something has been meeting at night near {place}, and they call on {god}.
The name of {god} began to be heard near {place}, where it ought not to be heard.
cult_purged: {church} rooted out a hidden cell of {cult} in {place}.
The faithful burned the secret shrine of {cult} near {place}.
{church} took the cell of {cult} at {place} apart.
There were arrests near {place}: {church} had found {cult} at last.
cult_incident: Graves opened in the night near {place}.
Strange lights and missing folk near {place}.
A priest was found dead in {place}, and no one will say how.
Something was left on the church step at {place}, and the priest burned it.
Two shepherds near {place} have not come back, and the dogs will not go that way.
gang_new: {gang} began to prey on the roads near {place}.
A new band of outlaws, {gang}, haunts the country near {place}.
Nobody rides alone near {place} now: {gang} have seen to that.
{gang} put up a toll of their own on the road by {place}.
gang_destroyed: {gang} were hunted down by the men of {lord}.
{lord}'s men finished {gang} in a barn, at dawn.
{gang} are gone; {lord} sent the heads round the villages.
dragon: {dragon} came out of the mountains and burned {place}.
{dragon} came down on {place}, and there was nothing to be done.
They saw {dragon} from three valleys away, and then {place} was alight.
dragon_tribute: {dragon} came to {place}. They drove out cattle and set out silver, and were spared.
{place} pays tribute to {dragon} now: beasts, gold, and once a year something worse.
{place} buys its life from {dragon} once a year, and does not talk about what with.
The tribute road to {dragon}'s lair starts at {place}, and is well worn.
dragon_slain: {dragon} was killed by {legend}, at a price.
{legend} killed {dragon}, and did not come home whole.
They brought the head of {dragon} down out of the hills; {legend} had done it.
dragon_sleeps: {dragon} went back to its lair and has not been seen since.
No one has seen {dragon} for many years. Some say it only sleeps.
{dragon} has not flown in living memory. Nobody is comforted.
The country near {dragon}'s lair has been quiet for years, which is its own kind of warning.
founded: Settlers raised the first houses of {place}.
The first stones of {place} were laid.
People settled at {place}, for the water and the road.
ruin: {place} fell to {cause} and was never rebuilt.
{cause} emptied {place}, and the roofs went in one winter.
Nobody rebuilt {place} after {cause}; the walls are still there.
legend: {legend} {deed}, and the songs have not let it go.
artifact: As for {artifact}: it {fate}, if the tellers are honest.
marriage: {a} and {b} were joined by a marriage.
{a} and {b} were married, and the lawyers were busier than the priest.
A wedding tied {a} and {b} together, whatever either of them wanted.
assassination: {victim} of {faction} was killed {cause}, and nobody was ever charged.
treaty: {a} and {b} swore a treaty of friendship.
{a} and {b} put their seals to an understanding.
{a} and {b} agreed to stand together, for as long as it suits.
beast_attack: {beast} came down on {place} in the night and killed {dead}.
{beast} killed {dead} at {place} and went back to its lair.
Word from {place}: {beast} has come down again and killed {dead}.
{place} is burying {dead} after {beast} came down from its lair.
{beast} is hunting again: {dead} dead at {place}, and the doors barred at dusk.
hero_died: They are burying {hero} at {place}; the hero died {cause}.
{hero} died {cause}, and {place} is quieter for it.
The bards of {place} have a last verse to sing: {hero} died {cause}.
chapter: The {people} of {faction} took a house in {place} and hung out their arms.

notices: Wanted: a strong back at the smithy. Pay by the day.
Lost: a grey nanny goat, answers to nothing. Reward.
Rooms to let, clean straw, no fleas (or not many). Ask at the inn.
The ferryman will not cross after dark. Do not ask him.
Found: one boot. Owner may have it back for a kind word.
Masses said for the dead of the last winter, every seventh day.
A reward to whoever finds who has been taking the chickens.
Do not drink from the east well. The priest says it is bad.
Carters wanted for the road south. Must bring their own axe.
The widow of {place}'s last tanner sells his tools. Cheap.
ruin_causes: a curse, or so they say
